title: Patrick Winston ·《How to Speak》— 天赋那一项很小
title_en: Patrick Winston · How to Speak — The T Is Very Small

questions.question: Patrick Winston 在《How to Speak》里说，提问后要等七秒，这是「标准」等待时间。回到等待时间研究的原始来源，实际情况是？
options: 测的是小学科学课：老师平均只等一秒，拉到三到五秒更好
原研究认为等待会让课堂冷场，建议老师尽快自己给出答案
原研究在大学讲堂测得最佳等待正是七秒，Winston 准确转述了它
原研究发现等待越久越好，七秒只是一个保守的下限
questions.explanation: Mary Budd Rowe 分析的是小学科学课录音：老师提问后平均约等一秒，训练后拉到三到五秒，学生回答更长、更主动。七秒在课上没有出处，这是 Winston 顺手挂上的数字普遍比原始研究说得满的一例。
questions.question_en: In 'How to Speak', Patrick Winston says to wait seven seconds after asking a question — the 'standard' wait time. What does the original wait-time research actually show?
options_en: It studied elementary science classes: teachers waited about one second, and stretching it to three to five improved answers
It found waiting kills momentum and advised teachers to supply the answer quickly
It measured an optimal wait of exactly seven seconds in university lectures, which Winston reported accurately
It found that longer is always better, with seven seconds as a conservative minimum
questions.explanation_en: Mary Budd Rowe analyzed recordings of elementary science lessons: teachers waited about a second on average, and when trained to wait three to five seconds, students gave longer and more spontaneous answers. Seven seconds has no source in the talk — one of several figures Winston stated more strongly than the research does.

questions.question: 按 Winston 的建议，一场求职报告的最后一页幻灯片应该放什么、最后一句话又该怎么说？
options: 最后一页写「贡献」呼应开头；结尾不说谢谢，而是向听众致敬
最后一页写「问题与讨论」；结尾总结时再把全部要点念一遍
最后一页写「结论」，概括主要发现；结尾说「谢谢聆听」以示礼貌
最后一页放合作者名单以示公平；结尾用一个笑话收住
questions.explanation: 「结论」多是正确但没人在乎的话，人们在乎的是你做了什么；合作者名单让人觉得你的那份工作被除以了一千，应放在第一页致谢。说「谢谢聆听」暗示大家熬到现在全凭礼貌，是一步弱棋；他自己以「我很高兴你们来了」向听众致敬。
questions.question_en: Following Winston's advice, what should the last slide of a job talk say, and how should the final words go?
options_en: Title it 'Contributions', echoing the steps listed at the start; don't end with thanks — salute the audience instead
Title it 'Questions and Discussion'; end by reading through all the key points again
Title it 'Conclusions' summarizing the findings; end with 'thank you for listening' to be polite
Show the list of collaborators to be fair; end with a joke
questions.explanation_en: 'Conclusions' are usually true things nobody cares about — people care what you did; a collaborator list makes your share look divided by a thousand, so acknowledge collaborators on the first slide. 'Thank you for listening' implies people stayed only out of politeness, a weak move; Winston himself ended by saying he was glad they came.

questions.question: 「手写笔记比键盘更好」的著名研究在直接复制中没站住。这对 Winston 课堂上禁止开电脑的规矩意味着什么？
options: 复制失败证明用电脑记笔记反而更好，应当鼓励开电脑
他的规矩随之失去了依据，因为它从头到尾建立在手写优于键盘之上
他的理由本是分心和干扰旁人，不是记笔记方式，这条仍有支持
复制失败说明电脑对课堂学习毫无影响，开不开都一样
questions.explanation: Winston 讲的理由是人只有一个语言处理器、会让周围人分心、会干扰讲者。Sana 等人 2013 年的实验显示，坐在开小差的电脑后面的学生测验正确率从 73% 降到 56%。复制失败只是说按记笔记方式区分差异很小且不显著，并不说明电脑无害——他的规矩比他的理由走得远，而理由本身没倒。
questions.question_en: The famous finding that longhand notes beat laptop notes didn't hold up in a direct replication. What does that mean for Winston's ban on open laptops in his lecture?
options_en: The failed replication proves laptop note-taking is better, so laptops should be encouraged
His rule loses its basis, since it rested entirely on handwriting beating typing
His reason was never note-taking method but distraction of oneself and neighbors, which still has experimental support
The failed replication shows laptops have no effect on classroom learning either way
questions.explanation_en: Winston's reasons were that people have one language processor, that laptops distract neighbors, and that they rattle the speaker. In Sana et al. (2013), students seated behind multitasking laptops scored 56% versus 73%. The replication found only a small, non-significant difference by note-taking method — not that laptops are harmless. His rule has spread further than his reasons, but the reasons still stand.
